description: Composite three-panel figure combining two SEM micrographs with an EDS spectrum of the SPSed Fe40Mn19Ni15Al15Si10C1 low-density high-entropy steel (MA 35 h, spark plasma sintered at 900 °C / 50 MPa). (a) is a lower-magnification SEM image with a 5 µm scale bar showing a light-grey matrix densely populated by submicron dark-grey to black particles plus scarce bright white particles, giving a granular, inhomogeneous contrast. (b) is a higher-magnification SEM image (3 µm scale bar) in which blue arrows label three contrast classes: 1 = light grey, 2 = white, 3 = dark grey; dark agglomerated features show an onion-like layered appearance. (c) is a red-filled full-area EDS spectrum of the area marked in (b): x-axis 0.00-9.00+ keV, y-axis 0-189 counts with gridlines every 21 counts; labelled peaks are C, Fe, Mn, Ni, Al and Si at low energy and Mn, Fe (Kα, the tallest peak), Mn, Fe and Ni at higher energies. Taken together, the panels demonstrate that all constituent elements survive MA + SPS and that the sintered pellet is chemically and microstructurally heterogeneous at the submicron scale, with several contrast classes attributed to distinct phases.

observations.observation: Panel (a) is an SEM micrograph carrying a 5 µm scale bar and shows a light-grey matrix containing numerous submicron dark grey/black particles and sparse bright white particles.
Panel (b) is an SEM micrograph with a 3 µm scale bar, i.e. higher magnification than (a), showing the same granular microstructure.
In (b) three blue arrows labelled 1, 2 and 3 point to distinct contrast regions of the microstructure.
The caption states the contrast classes are white (2), light grey (1) and dark grey (3).
The caption states that the shape of the black and dark grey features is onion type.

Panel (c) is an EDS spectrum plotted with X-ray energy on the abscissa from 0.00 to 9.00 keV (ticks at 1.00 keV intervals) and intensity on the ordinate from 0 to 189 counts with tick marks every 21 counts.
The EDS spectrum in (c) is filled red and its labelled peaks are C, Fe, Mn, Ni, Al and Si in the low-energy region and Mn, Fe, Mn, Fe and Ni at higher energies.
The tallest peak in the EDS spectrum (c) is labelled Fe and lies just above 6.0 keV on the energy axis; a second prominent Mn peak sits near 5.9 keV.
The caption states the EDS spectrum (c) is by full-area EDS analysis of the area marked in (b).

The citing text states the SEM micrographs of the SPSed sample were taken at 900 °C and 50 MPa and exhibit white, black, light and dark grey contrasts, which may correspond to BCC, B2-type, γ-brass-type and Fe5Si3-type intermetallic phases respectively.
The citing text states that all elements are present in the SEM-EDS full-area analysis of the SPSed pellet shown in Fig. 7(c).

The citing text (regarding Fig. 6) states that the SPSed sample is mainly BCC (ferrite) with partially ordered B2, trace γ-brass-type and Fe5Si3-type silicide phases, providing the phase context for the contrasts in (a) and (b).

The caption describes three contrast levels in the SEM images whereas the citing text lists four (white, black, light grey, dark grey); the panel pixels show at least a bright white, a light grey matrix and dark/black particles.

subfigures.description: Lower-magnification SEM micrograph of the SPSed HES with a 5 µm scale bar; light-grey matrix with abundant fine dark grey/black particles and occasional bright white particles, i.e. a fine granular multi-contrast microstructure.

Higher-magnification SEM micrograph (3 µm scale bar) of the same sample; three blue arrows labelled 1, 2 and 3 mark light grey, white and dark grey contrast regions respectively, and the dark features appear as layered onion-type agglomerates.

Red-filled EDS spectrum over 0.00-9.00+ keV (y-axis 0-189 counts, 21-count gridlines) from full-area analysis of the area marked in (b), with labelled peaks for C, Fe, Mn, Ni, Al, Si at low energy and Mn, Fe, Mn, Fe, Ni, Ni at higher energy; Fe Kα near 6.4 keV is the most intense peak.

unreadable_items: panel (c): no quantitative composition (at.% or wt.%) values are printed on the spectrum
panel (c): the minor high-energy Ni peak label near 8.2 keV is faint against the noisy baseline and only partially readable
panels (a) and (b): no phase identification labels are printed on the micrographs themselves; contrast-to-phase assignment comes only from the caption/citing text
